description_summary: 12-month unduplicated enrollment headcounts broken down by enrollment level, sex, and nine race/ethnicity categories. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS institution ID (UNITID) and enrollment level (EFFYLEV), with separate male, female, and combined headcounts.

12-month instructional activity measured in total credit hours and/or contact hours, broken down by undergraduate and graduate instructional level. The table provides institution-level activity measures used to derive 12-month full-time-equivalent enrollment; the supplied description does not name a separate record-key variable.

Awards conferred by 6-digit CIP program, first or second major, award level, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, CIPCODE, MAJORNUM, and AWLEVEL, and contains award counts by gender and nine race/ethnicity categories.

Students receiving any degree or certificate, broken down by race/ethnicity and gender. There is one record per institution, uniquely identified by UNITID; this table has no program or award-level grain and reports student counts rather than award counts.

Students receiving awards broken down by award level, race/ethnicity, gender, and age category. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and AWLEVEL; age counts cover under 18, 18–24, 25–39, and 40 or older, but race, gender, and age are not available in combination.

Programs offered and programs offered via distance education, broken down by CIP code and award level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and CIPCODE: 6-digit CIP records show award levels offered and offered via distance education, 2-digit CIP records summarize the 6-digit programs in the group, and CIPCODE 99 provides institution totals.

Fall enrollment counts by gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely defined by UNITID and EFLEVEL and includes total, male, and female counts overall and by attendance status.

Fall enrollment counts by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely defined by UNITID and EFALEVEL and includes total, male, and female counts for all nine race/ethnicity categories, overall and by attendance status.

Fall enrollment counts by distance-education status and student level. Each record is uniquely defined by UNITID and EFDELEV and reports total enrollment plus counts exclusively in distance education, in some distance education, or in none; exclusive-distance-education counts are further categorized by location relative to the institution, including same state, different state, unknown U.S. state, and outside the U.S.

Fall enrollment counts by age category, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely defined by UNITID, EFBAGE, and LSTUDY. Age enrollment reporting is optional in even-numbered years; 2013 is odd, so age data are collected under the catalog rule.

First-time freshman counts by state of residence, including the number who graduated from high school the previous year. Each record is uniquely defined by UNITID and EFCSTATE. Residence reporting is optional in odd-numbered years, so 2013 (odd) has data available but institutions may choose whether to report it.

Institution-level measures of total entering class, first-year retention rate, and student-to-faculty ratio, with each record keyed by UNITID. These measures apply only to institutions with undergraduate students; entering-class data are reported only by academic-year institutions, and short programs of less than one year do not have retention data.

Institution-level finance data for public institutions using GASB 34/35 accounting standards, including revenues by source, expenditures by category, and assets and liabilities. Query this table for the public-GASB population; public institutions using FASB are reported separately.

Institution-level finance data for private not-for-profit institutions and public institutions using FASB accounting standards, including revenues by source, expenditures by category, and assets and liabilities. Query this table for the private-not-for-profit population or the subset of public institutions that use FASB rather than GASB.

Institution-level finance data for private for-profit institutions using FASB accounting standards, including revenues by source, expenditures by category, and assets and liabilities. Query this table for the private for-profit population; it is separate from both private not-for-profit institutions and public institutions.

Graduation outcomes at 200% of normal time, covering 2005 bachelor’s-degree-seeking cohorts at four-year institutions and 2009 cohorts at less-than-4-year institutions. It includes enrollment and completion within 100%, 150%, or 200% of normal time; four-year records are restricted to bachelor’s degree seekers, while less-than-4-year records cover students seeking any degree or certificate.

Graduation outcomes at 150% of normal time for 2007 cohorts at four-year institutions and 2010 cohorts at two-year institutions, broken down by gender and race/ethnicity. Records are uniquely defined by IPEDS ID (UNITID), cohort and graduation status (GRTYPE); the table includes bachelor’s-degree-seeking and other degree/certificate-seeking cohorts at four-year institutions and transfer-out outcomes, while two-year records include completion at 100% or 150% and transfer-out. Two-year completion within 100% of normal time is not available by gender and race/ethnicity.

Graduation outcomes at 150% of normal time for the 2010 cohort at less-than-2-year institutions, including institution-level counts enrolled, completing within 100% or 150% of normal time, or transferring out. This table is restricted to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at less-than-2-year institutions.

Staff counts by full- or part-time status, medical-school status, occupational category, faculty status, tenure status, and contract type. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EAPCAT, which combines occupational category and tenure status.

Counts of full-time instructional staff by faculty and tenure status, academic rank, race/ethnicity, gender, and contract type for degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SISCAT, which combines FACSTAT with academic rank.

Counts of full-time new hires by primary occupational category, race/ethnicity, and gender for degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices; instructional new hires also have faculty/tenure-status detail. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SNHCAT, which combines primary occupation with instructional faculty/tenure status. Reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2013 (odd) has data under that rule.

Full- and part-time staff counts by occupational category, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and STAFFCAT, which combines occupational category with full- or part-time status.

Counts of full-time instructional staff by academic rank, faculty status, tenure status, and contract type for degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and FACSTAT, the combined faculty/tenure-status category; rank counts are included within each record.

Counts and salary outlays for full-time nonmedical instructional staff, broken down by academic rank, gender, and 9-, 10-, 11-, or 12-month contract length. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and ARANK; the table also provides total months and weighted average monthly salary by rank and gender.

Counts and salary outlays for full-time nonmedical noninstructional staff by occupational category. Records are at the institution-by-occupational-category level, identified by UNITID and the occupational-category field.

Custom comparison-group membership records for the 2014 Data Feedback Report, identifying each submitting institution and its comparison institutions by UNITID, with institution name and state; the grain is submitting institution plus comparison-group member.

Institution-by-survey-component response records keyed by UNITID and survey component, showing response, nonresponse with imputation, applicability, parent/child or multi-campus reporting, and revised-submission status in final or revised releases.

Institution directory records keyed by UNITID, containing institution names and locations, active and Title IV participation indicators, institutional URLs, and characteristics such as control, level, highest award offered, and Carnegie classification.

Institution-level records keyed by UNITID covering educational offerings, award levels, organization, control and affiliation, special learning opportunities, services, and athletic associations; applicant, admission, and test-score fields are limited to institutions without open admission.

Institution-level academic-year charge records keyed by UNITID for primarily academic, credit-hour institutions using semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or another academic calendar. Fields include average tuition and required fees for full-time undergraduate and graduate students, per-credit charges for part-time students, charges for specified professional-practice programs, and full-time first-time undergraduate price-of-attendance components.

Vocational-program charge records for institutions using clock hours or primarily occupational credit-hour programs, reported for the full program length rather than an academic year. The grain is institution plus program record: the largest program and up to five additional programs, with program counts, tuition and fees, books and supplies, and price-of-attendance fields for entering students.
Institution-level mission-statement records keyed by UNITID, containing either the institution’s mission text or the web address where it is available.

Student financial aid recipients and aid amounts broken down by undergraduate population, aid type, and aid source. Rows are defined by institution, student population, and aid category/source, with recipient counts plus total and average dollars; the detailed source breakdown applies to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates, while the all-undergraduate measures cover total grants, Pell grants, and federal loans.

Average net price and the underlying financial-aid measures for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates, broken down into grant-and-scholarship recipients versus Title IV federal-aid recipients and reported for 2010-11, 2011-12, and 2012-13. Rows are defined by institution, student group, and academic year; at public institutions, both groups are limited to students paying in-district or in-state tuition.
